note: Recent work is listed first. Earlier dates cover selected milestones reconstructed from saved reports and project notes; they are not a complete activity history.

items.text: Trained logistic and neural classifiers on the prepared speech examples. With the same whole-claim check, logistic regression gets 77 of 86 and the five neural runs get 76–77. The frozen combination gets 80.
items.label: Learned speech relation scores

items.text: Prepared 104 training and 62 calibration examples for spoken alternatives from five AMI recordings outside the earlier evaluations. Reviewed both wordings and edits, checked the source split, and cached frozen DeBERTa vectors.
items.label: Speech relation training data

items.text: Checked whether a speech span relates the options in the claim. Combining this check with whole-claim scoring gives 35 of 38 new decisions, compared with 32 for the earlier method.
items.label: Specific speech options

items.text: Compared aggregation on eight original frames with natural occlusion or small objects. All three methods agree on the decisions, including a miss on shields partly obscured by smoke.
items.label: Naturally difficult frames

items.text: Scored whether speakers present alternatives in 24 fixed excerpts. Qwen improves the grounded comparison from 39 to 44 of 48 decisions. Two changed options still get false support.
items.label: Speech alternatives and remaining errors

items.text: Compared three ways of scoring several distinct pairs on five real frames. Exact inference accounts for reused regions and all three methods agree on the 20 decisions.
items.label: Overlapping visual assignments

items.text: Tested speech without explicit “or” on 12 unused AMI recordings. Same-span binding reduces raw false support from ten to three and keeps seven valid reports. The wording check misses all eight.
items.label: Implicit alternatives

items.text: Compared exact inference with the best assignment on five visual and OCR frame pairs. The methods agree on all 20 decisions. Constructed controls show when several scores can change a decision and when repeated evidence should count once.
items.label: Visual and OCR assignments

items.text: Compared speaker and utterance binding on eight AMI utterances and 32 controls. Requiring one utterance matched 40 of 40 verdicts. Three usable compiled programs passed all 15 exact inference checks.
items.label: Binding controls and compiled programs

items.text: Compared two diarizers on the same clips. Three Pyannote windows recover one additional query with mixed speakers. Reverb supports one of eight, the same as the earlier baseline.
items.label: Automatic speaker windows

items.text: Compared frozen transcript scorers on the same eight annotated windows. Whole-utterance DeBERTa matches 26 of 32 judgments and accepts six edits. Sixteen claims preserve the required speaker and reported content in the compiler.
items.label: Scorer and compiler examples

items.text: Used target-interval speaker annotations to diagnose automatic attribution. Each diarizer recovers one clean match. Both retain every word in one candidate for only two of eight utterances before speaker naming.
items.label: Speaker attribution examples

items.text: Compared speaker-turn windows on 24 unused AMI meeting series. Keeping overlaps retains all target words in 18 before naming and zero with names assigned from earlier speech.
items.label: Window cases

items.text: Calibrated frozen DeBERTa scores on one group of meetings and tested on another. Correct decisions rise from 37 to 41 of 48 on the initial test wording and to 42 after wording corrections.
items.label: Held-out speech cases

items.text: Compared five methods on 96 speech queries with the same annotated transcripts. Shared binding raised calibrated decisions from 72 to 89. The simple filter matched DeepProbLog on every query.
items.label: Paired binding examples

items.text: Audited 48 directly quoted claims. The compiler retained 32 as verbatim speech and abstained on the multi-sentence quotations.
items.label: Automatic compilation

items.text: Audited 35 claims with standalone “or” outside quotes and tested inclusive OR with fixed evidence. Reviewed lost alternatives, modifier attachment and reported speech.
items.label: OR examples

items.text: Fixed AMR conversion of the pier or terminal area claim. The fixed sequence now passes 2,178 of 2,375 checks. All 2,177 earlier programs are byte-identical.
items.label: Comparison

items.text: Tested a parallel rewrite with explicit OR. It compiles when each branch preserves its source modifiers. The AND version and the version that adds modifiers to the terminal branch are refused.
items.label: Rewrite controls

items.text: One local Qwen response per remaining failure. All five emitted OR. Zero passed because of scope, component compilation or a repeated formula leaf.
items.label: Five rewrite results

items.text: Evaluated 12 authored claims. Eight programs passed checks, four matched the reference, three were partial, one was incorrect and four had no program. The incorrect pass omits explicit exclusion.
items.label: Twelve evaluation cases

items.text: Ran 26 exact inference controls on reference forms and two on compiled forms. The controls show correct exclusion and how a partially observed report can receive support if the report condition is assumed supported.
items.label: Inference controls

items.text: Implemented explicit exclusion, same-entity and shared-time alternatives, and a speech predicate for the full reported OR. All 12 development cases compile. Ten match their readings and two are partial.
items.label: Before and after

items.text: The corpus rerun passes 2,179 of 2,375 claims. All 2,178 prior programs are byte-identical. The new pass preserves the purpose of crouching or sitting.
items.label: Shared conditions

items.text: Passed 26 exact inference controls on compiled forms. The speech test distinguishes complete reports, single assertions and incomplete transcripts. The rewrite test checks that the shared condition binds to the same truck.
items.label: Evidence controls

items.text: Compared three ways to check reported OR on 58 pairs from eight AMI recordings and controlled edits. The alternative comparison matches 54 judgments and whole-utterance entailment matches 42. Three compiled speech conditions support 18 exact DeepProbLog checks.
items.label: Transcript evidence

items.text: Ran the fixed direct compiler on 16 AVeriTeC claims from fresh source pages. Ten pass the checks, two match the frozen reading, and six produce no program. Negation and shared words across alternatives are exposed as remaining errors.
items.label: New-source cases

items.text: Fixed negation over OR and two kinds of shared content, and recovered one reported alternative. Both original errors are repaired. All 2,179 earlier corpus programs are byte-identical.
items.label: Logical form changes

items.text: Checked genuine alternatives worded without “or,” plus crops, speaker and time shifts, and edited claims. The revised check matches 32 of 32 expected judgments, with speaker and timing supplied.
items.label: Transcript cases

items.text: Reviewed 12 new claim texts. Seven compile, and one fully matches the reading. “Without,” consequences and swapped roles remain. The targeted repair and transcript checks meet their stopping criteria.
items.label: Fresh claim audit

items.text: Tested shared absence and consequences on 33 texts. Both earlier scope errors are repaired, and two new false passes now abstain. All 2,179 accepted corpus programs replay byte-for-byte.
items.label: Scope examples

items.text: Ran CPU diarization on eight fresh AMI meetings. Correct-speaker support falls from eight with the annotated windows to one with automatic speaker windows. Providing the participant count leaves the verdict counts unchanged.
